newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Yam says markets appear confident about Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Yam says markets appear confident about Hong Kong.

text.p: Joseph Yam, chief executive of Hong Kong Monetary Authority, said markets are giving a confident message about Hong Kong's handover to China in July of this year.

"There won't be any significant changes to Hong Kong's monetary arrangements after 1997," said Yam, speaking to reporters here before the start of a meeting at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
"Markets are giving a clear message," Yam said, refering to a 30 percent gain in the Hong Kong stock markets last year.
He added price/earnings ratios were between 13 and 14 on average, lower than for other Asian markets.
He said this could indicate that the markets would return to normal following the handover.
Regarding the bond market, Yam said the HKMA, the defacto central bank of Hong Kong, paid a premium of 40 basis points above U.S. rates on 10-year paper.
"This represents credit risk compared with America, and also currency risks," he said.
"Forty basis points really is very small, so markets are giving a very clear message that confidence in Hong Kong after 1997 is very high," he said.
